questions.question: Which secret-management standard should we adopt for harness/skill secrets (drives what we implement on #14)?

options.label: macOS Keychain
options.description: Match the existing remote_control pattern (security find-generic-password). Strong, zero deps, but macOS-only and NOT synced across your macbook + macmini (provision each host).

options.label: CredentialManager lib
options.description: Promote fin-export/finex/credentials.py to a shared lib: env / Fernet-encrypted YAML / keyring. Encrypted-file option syncs across hosts. Adds cryptography+keyring deps.

options.label: 1Password CLI
options.description: Use `op read op://...`. Built-in cross-host sync, audit, sharing. Requires a 1Password subscription + the op CLI installed/authed.

options.label: Tiered policy only
options.description: Keep plaintext .env for low-sensitivity/local keys (incl. the Adzuna trial key); require Keychain only for sensitive secrets. Lowest friction; least change.

options.description: Click 'Create new key' on Adzuna, revoke the exposed one. I install the fresh key into whatever store we pick. Clean slate.

transcript_tail.text: I now have the full picture. Let me verify one thing about the board items (draft vs real issues) so I wire the dependency correctly.

Here's what I found, and it directly shapes the discussion. Let me set up the ticket + dependency first, then lay out the options.

**Current state — three secret patterns coexist, no unified policy:**

| Repo | Mechanism | Security tier |
|---|---|---|
| **ai-harness** (`remote_control`) | macOS **Keychain** — `security find-generic-password -s "Claude Code-credentials" -w`, read fresh each cycle, never logged, never written to disk | ✅ strong (the baseline) |
| **fin-export** (`finex/credentials.py`) | `CredentialManager` abstraction: env vars / **Fernet-encrypted YAML** / system **keyring** | ✅ strong, pluggable |
| **job-search** (`.env`) | **plaintext** `.env`, gitignored ← *the Adzuna key I just wrote* | ⚠️ weakest (cleartext on disk) |
| **FamilyFund** (`app1/.env`) | plaintext `.env`, gitignored (Laravel default) | ⚠️ weak |

So the harness already has a strong Keychain pattern — but the Adzuna key defaulted to the weakest tier, which is the inconsistency you're flagging. Board #3 items are *draft* issues (no number to link), and real issues live in `ai-harness`/board #2, so I'll create the secret-management ticket there as a proper linkable issue.

Let me create it.
Issue **#14** created. Now add it to board #2, and revert the Adzuna draft on board #3 (Done → Todo) with a blocker note so the dependency is visible.
The status revert worked. The title/body edit needs the draft's `DI_` content id (not the `PVTI_` item id). Let me fetch it and verify the board #2 add.
#14 is on board #2 (Todo). Now annotate the Adzuna draft with the correct `DI_` id.

Everything is set up. Here's where we are:

## ✅ Paused + tracked + dependency wired

- **Created** `ai-harness#14` — *"Unify secret management across harness repos"* → on board **#2** (Todo). Body has the full audit + open questions.
- **Reverted** the Adzuna ticket (board #3) Done → **Todo**, retitled *"… (BLOCKED by ai-harness#14)"*, body notes it's paused on a plaintext key.
- **Not touched:** `job-search/.env` stays as-is so the skill still works if you want it; no further job-search build-out until #14 is decided.

## 🔐 The discussion

**One hygiene note first:** the Adzuna key is now in *this chat transcript* (you pasted the dashboard screenshot, and it's in `.env`). It's a low-sensitivity free *trial* key (read-only job search, no PII/money), so this is minor — but if you want strict hygiene, Adzuna's "Create new key" rotates it in one click and we install the fresh one wherever we land.

**The real question is the going-forward standard.** Realistic options, grounded in what you already run:

| Option | How it works | Cross-host (mbp+mini) | Cost/friction |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. macOS Keychain** | `security add/find-generic-password` — same as `remote_control` today | ❌ not synced; provision per host | none; macOS-only |
| **B. fin-export `CredentialManager` as shared lib** | env / Fernet-encrypted YAML / `keyring` | ✅ via encrypted YAML (sync the file, provision the Fernet key once) | adds `cryptography`/`keyring` deps |
| **C. Tiered policy** | plaintext `.env` OK for low-sensitivity/local-only; Keychain required for sensitive | n/a | lowest; you define the line |
| **D. 1Password CLI (`op`)** | `op read "op://vault/item/field"` | ✅ built-in sync + audit | needs 1Password sub + `op` |

My read: you already have **A** (Keychain) and **B** (CredentialManager) in the codebase, so the cheapest coherent move is to **pick one as the standard and migrate to it**, with **C** as the written policy for what *doesn't* need it. The cross-host constraint (two Macs, keychains don't sync) is the deciding factor — if that matters, A alone won't cut it.
